text:
Ravi (PM): Quick thread to lock the private-deploy launch shape. We have to pick defaults for installers, networking, and key management by EOD. Keep replies short.

Claire (Field): Summary from three customers: 1) wants a single tarball they can validate offline; 2) wants stable egress for allowlists (sticky IP or NAT preserve); 3) wants minimal manual steps — a one-page install checklist.

Liam (Eng): Technical tradeoffs: full bundle (images included) => simpler airgap installs but huge artifact size and slower downloads. Registry-first with presigned images => smaller distribution, easier CI, but adds presigned flow and transient registry access for some customers.

Hana (Security): KMS stance: support customer-managed CMEK/KMS for GA. HSM can be opt-in enterprise. Also require an installer permission checklist (least-privilege) surfaced during install.

Claire (Field): Also ask for three reference network diagrams: behind NAT, preserved-eip, and direct peering. Customers love diagrams.

Ravi (PM): Proposal: GA = registry-first installer + generated offline tarball workflow (tooling to produce tarball from registry for customers who need it). Default networking = NATed egress, but include IP-preserve addon in docs + script. KMS = CMEK support GA; HSM v1.1. Thoughts?

Liam (Eng): Implementation notes: add 'bundleize' helper that pulls images and emits tarball + sha256 manifest. That helper can live in repo and be run by CI or by customers. Effort ~1wk eng + 1wk QA. Rolling upgrades require operator to support annotate-pause + pre-apply validation; add a drain/rehydration hook for cache heavy nodes.

Claire (Field): Field preference = Ravi's proposal. Customers prefer smaller regular updates and a simple tool to create airgap artifacts.

Hana (Security)::+1: for CMEK GA. Please add a short threat model snippet in the tarball README (how to verify signature, required IAM roles).

Ravi (PM): Ok consensus for registry-first + tarball-tool path. Action items: Liam to create RDW-1510 (bundleize helper) and RDW-1511 (one-page install checklist + network diagrams). Claire to gather exact firewall rules from pilots. Hana to draft KMS perms snippet. Ops-bot: create tasks.

ops-bot: Created RDW-1510, RDW-1511, and RDW-1512 (installer perms checklist).

Liam (Eng): Quick Q: do we default the installer to attempt registry pull, then fallback to local tar? Or require explicit flag? My vote: try registry, but error guidance should clearly show how to run bundleize locally.

Claire (Field): Explicit flag is safer for airgapped installs. Customers often run explicit workflows.

Ravi (PM): Decision: installer default = registry-pull. Add --offline flag to force tarball mode and surface presigned-image flow in output. We'll document both.

Hana (Security): Also add a signed-manifest step for tarballs (GPG or sigstore) so customers can verify.

Liam (Eng): Agreed. I'll add sig verification and manifest validation to helper.

Ravi (PM): Thanks all. I'll update the roadmap notes and mark this as GA shape. If anyone objects, speak now or we'll lock by EOD.
